newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka tenders to buy early Sept 1.0-pct diesel.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tenders to buy early Sept 1.0-pct diesel.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 1.0 percent sulphur diesel for September 3-4 delivery, cost-and-freight Colombo, a CPC source said on Wednesday.
The tender closes at 1500 hours Sri Lanka time on August 13 and offers will be valid for two days.
This is the second time in a row that CPC has not included jet fuel in its tender.

In its last tender for August 11-12 delivery, CPC bought 250,000 barrels of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel from Swiss trader Glencore at a 68-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Colombo.
That was the only cargo Sri Lanka purchased for August delivery.
The source said Sri Lanka is taking less diesel and jet fuel now because its stocks are high as power stations are using more hydropower for generation amid the heavy rains.

This was markedly different from May and June when a drought and an unexpected shutdown of the 55,000-barrel-per-day Sapugaskanda refinery, forced Sri Lanka to import six combination cargoes of diesel and jet fuel for the two months.
CPC took two combination cargoes in July, which is its normal monthly imports.
